info.title: Divinci Public/Customer API
info.description: Public API for managing whitelabels, RAG knowledge bases, releases, fine-tuning, transcripts, and more. This spec is auto-generated from the Express route definitions in workspace/servers/public-api/src/api/v1. Every path here is served; a small number of served routes are not yet extracted (see docs/api/openapi-coverage.md for the exact count).

tags.name: chat
tags.description: `POST /api/v1/chat/completions` is an OpenAI-style completions endpoint for calling a Divinci release with the request shape OpenAI clients already send. Needs `transcript:write`.

tags.name: connectors
tags.description: Third-party source connections: list providers and connections, start a provider's auth flow, read and update its settings, disconnect, and run, poll or cancel syncs. Includes the web-crawl and WordPress starters. `connector:read` for reads, `connector:write` for changes. Stored provider secrets are never returned in plain text.

tags.name: divinci-agent
tags.description: Internal service-to-service endpoints for the Divinci Agent worker. Everything except `GET /health` requires the internal `x-internal-api-key` header, not a customer API key.

tags.name: export
tags.description: Whitelabel configuration as a file: `GET /api/v1/export` exports it (JSON or YAML, `whitelabel:read`); `POST /api/v1/export` imports one (`whitelabel:write`).

tags.name: html-pages
tags.description: Read-only access to crawled web pages: list, count, look up by URL or id, and per-host listings and crawl history. This group is read-only; pages are added by crawling (for example the web-crawl connector). Needs `rag:read`.

tags.name: mcp-config
tags.description: Internal: the MCP worker resolves a whitelabel's MCP settings here. Authenticated by the origin pre-shared key, not a customer API key.

tags.name: notifications
tags.description: In-app notifications: list them, read unread counts, and mark one read (`PATCH /api/v1/notifications/{notificationId}/read`). `notification:read` / `notification:write`.

tags.name: rag
tags.description:
Knowledge bases (RAG vectors): create and tune indexes (`/rag/targets`), upload and manage files (`/rag/files`), group indexes (`/rag/groups`), and retrieve.

**Retrieval only, no generated answer:** `POST /api/v1/rag/context` returns the same chunks chat would put in the model's context for a query — use it to feed your own LLM. `GET /api/v1/rag/search` is keyword (full-text) search across the workspace's indexes. Both need an API key with `rag:read`.

tags.name: tts
tags.description: Text-to-speech: `POST /api/v1/tts/generate` synthesizes audio (`whitelabel:write`); `GET`/`PATCH /api/v1/tts/settings` read and update the workspace's TTS settings.

tags.name: voiceprints
tags.description: `GET /api/v1/voiceprints` lists the workspace's voiceprints. Needs `rag:read`. Voiceprints are biometric data; scope keys that can read them accordingly.

ApiKeyAuth.name: x-api-key
ApiKeyAuth.description: API key with format `divinci_...` (91 chars). Permissions are attached to each key; an EMPTY permissions array means full access within the whitelabel.

BearerAuth.description: Auth0 JWT token for workspace CRUD operations.

Unauthorized.description: Authentication required or API key invalid

RateLimitExceeded.description: Rate limit exceeded for this API key + feature

releaseId.description: A release whose assistant config drives this participant's turns.

assistantId.description: Or a bare model/assistant id (no release environment).

label.description: Display label shown in the UI / used for

enabled.description: Whether AI Gateway is enabled for this whitelabel/release

gatewayId.description: Gateway ID to use - either 'default' for Divinci's gateway or a custom gateway ID

useDefaultGateway.description:
Whether to use the default Divinci AI Gateway
If false, gatewayId must be provided

useWhiteLabelDefaults.description: For releases only - whether to use whitelabel's AI Gateway settings

customAccountId.description: Optional custom Cloudflare account ID if using custom gateway

cacheTtlSeconds.description:
Per-request cache TTL (seconds) sent as `cf-aig-cache-ttl` when routing
through the gateway. Bounds staleness; identical conversation-starter
requests re-hit within it. Omit → DEFAULT_AIG_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS (3600).

requested.description: What the variant asked for. null when no override configured.

used.description:
What's actually running. For "release-default" sources this is the
release's configured assistant. For "variant-override" it matches requested.

similarityThreshold.description: Minimum cosine similarity to consider a cache hit (default: 0.92)

scoresByVariant.description: Keyed by variantIndex-as-string. null = variant didn't run this test or errored.

errorsSample.description:
Truncated sample of the actual per-test error messages when errorCount>0.
Without this the CLI/report only shows errorCount and the real cause is
buried in the (composite-id, un-fetchable) QATestResult — making arena
generation failures undebuggable. Bounded to keep the report payload small.

chatBlockedUntilVendorBaa.description:
True while no model provider is BAA-covered, so a workspace scoped now
cannot chat yet. Forms render the "chat will pause" consequence from this
rather than hard-coding it.

enabled.description: Enable BM25 keyword search for hybrid retrieval

boost.description: Score boost multiplier for BM25 results (default: 2.0)

anonymousSessionId.description:
Set when this Chat is a persisted ANONYMOUS conversation (DrFurman-style
stateless anonymous chat, captured for analytics + feedback-conversation
links). The stable per-visitor session id is the upsert key — one Chat
per session, its transcript replaced with the latest each turn.
`ownerUser` is a sentinel ("anon:<sessionId>") since there's no auth user.
The visitor's email is intentionally NOT stored here (it lives only on
the message-feedback notification) to bound the PII footprint.

lastActivityAt.description: Epoch ms of the last turn — for analytics / recency sorting.

aiParticipants.description:
Conversational multi-AI roster. When present with >= 2 entries (and the
release's `multiAi.enabled` is true), a user message drives a bounded
round-robin exchange among these participants instead of a single reply.
Owner-managed. See AIChatParticipant.

parentChat.description:
Sub-thread linkage. When a user clicks "Send" on a product sub-reply in
the right-hand drawer of /ai-chat/:chatId, we lazily create a NEW
AIChat doc with this field set, pointing back at the parent chat +
the specific message whose sub-replies spawned it. The list-chats
query filters out chats where this is set, so child sub-thread chats
don't clutter the sidebar — they live inside the parent chat's
sub-thread drawer. Users can promote one to a full top-level chat via
the Expand button, which creates a separate independent fork (see
forkedFromSubThread).

forkedFromSubThread.description:
If this chat was produced by the Expand-to-fork action on a sub-thread
(full copy of the parent transcript + sub-thread messages), this points
back at the source for breadcrumbing. The forked chat itself is
independent and IS visible in the main chat list.

title.description: Card heading, e.g. "Interested in real estate investing?"

buttonLabel.description: Button label, e.g. "Get instant access". Optional; a sensible default is used when unset.

triggerKeywords.description:
Case-insensitive keywords/phrases scanned against the generated reply text.
First match (any keyword) triggers the card. Kept simple on purpose — one
CTA competing against nothing, so no BM25/alias machinery.

intervalMessages.description:
Fire on every Nth assistant reply (interval modes). E.g. 4 = the 4th, 8th,
12th… assistant reply is eligible. Required when triggerMode includes
"interval".

minMessagesBeforeFirst.description: Don't fire before the Nth assistant reply in the thread (1-based).

maxPerThread.description: Max fires per thread. Absent/0 = 1 (v1 once-per-thread).

cooldownMessages.description: Min assistant replies between two fires when maxPerThread > 1.

imageUrl.description: Optional thumbnail (e.g. a book cover), rendered beside the card text.

targetUrl.description: Destination opened in a new tab. Required for ctaType "link-out".

assetUrl.description: The gated asset (e.g. a PDF in R2) revealed/delivered after submit.

successMessage.description: Confirmation copy shown after a successful email submit.

crmDestination.description: Which CRM destination the captured lead is routed to (reuses the CRM-ingest pipeline).

constantContactListId.description:
Optional double-write: the customer's OWN Constant Contact list id. When
both this and `constantContactAccessToken` are set, a successful lead
submit also upserts the contact into the customer's Constant Contact
account (in addition to our own CRM ingest above), so their native email
automation fires. Absent → no double-write (default).

formFields.description: Which fields the inline form collects. Absent = ["email"]. Email is always required.

consentText.description: Consent/disclaimer line rendered under the inline form.

requireCaptcha.description: Require a Turnstile solve on submit (uses the FreeChatGate turnstile infra).

Write-only: `select: false` server-side, and API responses never echo it

update to keep the existing value; send "" to explicitly clear it).

version.description: Current revision number; starts at 1 and advances on each content change.

versionHistory.description: Prior revisions, oldest first. Appended by the update route.

translations.description:
Per-language translations of `message`, keyed by platform language
code (e.g. "es", "zh-hans"). The base `message` is the authoring
source; entries here are served when a chat requests that language
and the release supports it (see resolveSupportedLanguageCodes).

label.description: Human label for the model whose vindex is currently being edited.

affectsLiveChat.description: True once chat actually serves from edits (Phase 3). Honest default: false.

cadenceDays.description: Roll-up interval in days: 1 (daily), 3, or 7 (weekly). Default 1.

minFilesForRelease.description: Minimum files synced in the window to fork a draft release. Default 10.

lastChangelogAt.description: Last time the changelog roll-up ran for this whitelabel.

suiteId.description: Explicit suite; defaults to the workspace's most recent suite.

maxTests.description: Test cap for the mini run. Default 5.

autoQA.description:
Opt-in mini Scored QA against each auto-created draft release.
Costs real scorer-LLM money, so it ships off.

targetTypes.description:
Processing pipelines chosen at connect time. Auto-sync builds its sync
jobs from this; absent means RAG only.

url.description: R2 CDN URL for the image

altText.description: Alt text from the markdown image syntax

explicitTtlMinutes.description: Hard TTL for explicit caches in minutes. Default 60, range 5-360. Ignored when adaptiveTtl is true.

adaptiveTtl.description: When true, the server picks TTL from rolling traffic (target storage cost ≈ 5% of weekly savings).

cacheSystemPrompt.description: Cache the system prompt + tools as their own CachedContent resource. Default true when mode=explicit.

cacheGroundingDocs.description: Cache long RAG grounding documents (Phase 4). Default false; flip on per-Release once that lands.

stableRagOrdering.description:
Order retrieved RAG chunks deterministically (by vectorId, then content)
instead of by per-query relevance score, so queries with overlapping
retrieval share a byte-identical systemInstruction prefix → Google's
implicit cache fires across them. Default false: it trades relevance
ordering for cross-query prefix reuse, so enable per-Release and measure
savings (scripts/gemini-cache-savings-report.py) before broad rollout.

failClosed.description:
Failure mode when de-identification is enabled but the engine errors or is
unreachable (e.g. Presidio cold-start timeout, 5xx, network failure).

customPatterns.description: Custom regex patterns for domain-specific PII.

kind.description:
"embed" = platform-player iframe (YouTube/Vimeo/Wistia) resolved via
the ffmpeg container's yt-dlp endpoint (P3).

fileId.description: RagVectorFile2 id once ingestion was triggered.

vertexVectorId.description: Auto-created Vertex AI V2 RAG vector ID

embeddingDimension.description: Embedding dimension for Vertex AI V2 (default: 1500)

cartUrlPattern.description:
Cart URL pattern with placeholders: {sku}, {qty}, {variant_id}
Example: "https://shop.example.com/cart.php?action=add&sku={sku}&qty={qty}"

showPricing.description: Whether to show pricing in product recommendations

showMemberPricing.description: Whether to show member pricing for non-members (upsell)

preferSubscription.description: Default to subscription variant when available

referrerParam.description: Referrer parameter to append to product URLs

patchSetShas.description:
The patch sets the run's answers were ACTUALLY generated through (from
each result's modelEdits). One entry for a clean run; more than one means
the stack changed mid-run; empty means nothing was recorded (results
before 2026-09-27, or answers not generated through model edits). This,
not the pinned version, is what a before/after comparison must key on.

fileIdMap.description: Maps sourceFileId → newFileId. Useful for remapping ScoredQATest provenance.

authKeyTarget.description: The target `authKey` lives on, when it is NOT this fine-tune's own target.

mode.description:
Verification flow that must complete before any chat message is
served:
  - "none" — no gate; behaves like today's anonymous-chat. Useful
    for SDK consumers that want the platform quota engine without
    the email-verification UX.
  - "captcha-only" — Turnstile widget gates each session. No
    email collected. Bot-deterrent only.
  - "captcha+otp" — Turnstile + email + 6-digit OTP. Used by the
    Divinci.ai homepage today (v1 reference impl).
  - "captcha+magic-link" — Turnstile + email + click-through link.
    Used by DrFurman.ai today; lower visitor friction but depends
    on inbox delivery + click latency.

perEmailLifetime.description:
Total messages a single normalized email can send across its
lifetime BEFORE verification has completed. After verification,
additional `postVerifyWindowCount` messages unlock per rolling
`postVerifyWindowHours`-window. Default 1 in the email modes; 22 in
"captcha-only", where there is no verification and this cap is the
whole allowance (see `defaultFreeChatGateQuota`).

postVerifyWindowHours.description:
After verification, the rolling window in which the visitor can
send up to `postVerifyWindowCount` additional messages. Default
24 hours.

postVerifyWindowCount.description:
Max messages per rolling window for verified visitors. Default
5.

perDeviceLifetime.description:
Per-"device" lifetime cap. Always applied regardless of mode —
stops a single bot host from churning through fresh emails.
Default 3.

lifetimeResetHours.description:
Optional reset cadence for the two LIFETIME counters (`perEmailLifetime`
and `perDeviceLifetime`). Unset / 0 = never reset (the old behaviour: a
visitor who exhausts the allowance is locked out until the counter's
90-day TTL). Set to 24 for a daily refill or 168 for weekly.

quota.description:
Quota engine knobs. All counters key on the normalizedEmail-hash
(or device-hash for the per-device backstop) in Redis. INCR-on-
success-then-EXPIRE-on-first-write; fail-open on Redis error.

fromName.description: Display name used in the "From:" header. Default "Divinci".

fromAddress.description:
Sender address. Must be a domain verified at the email provider
(Resend in v1). Default "noreply@mail.divinci.ai".

welcomeCopy.description: Copy on the "check your email" screen.

successCopy.description: Copy on the post-verification success page.

brand.description:
Per-Release branding overrides for the verification email/UI.
Falls back to platform defaults when unset.

hubspot.description: HubSpot target. Omit to skip HubSpot.

attio.description: Attio target. Omit to skip Attio.

crm.description:
Optional CRM ingest target. When set, OTP-verified emails for this
Release are upserted (fire-and-forget) into the configured CRM(s) by
the gate's verify step — see server-resources globals/crm. Unset → no
ingest (the multi-tenant default, so e.g. a partner's gated emails are
never synced to Divinci's CRM). Marketing-contact status is set only
when the visitor opts in via the consent checkbox.

siteKey.description: BYO public sitekey (or a platform-widget override). Public, safe to serve.

secretRef.description: BYO secret reference — an env/Infisical key NAME, never the raw secret.

completedActions.description:
Tracks completed actions for deduplication and cap enforcement.
Each entry is an action key (e.g., "create_first_release").
Repeatable actions appear multiple times up to their cap.

chatBlockedUntilVendorBaa.description:
True when the workspace is now HIPAA-scoped but no model provider is
BAA-covered, so chat will refuse. Surfaced so the UI can say so at the
moment of acceptance rather than leaving the operator to discover it.

optionAvailable.description: False while the BAA is a counsel-unapproved draft: nothing can be accepted yet.

enableIntentDetection.description: Enable query intent detection for adaptive retrieval

enableTreePruning.description: Enable tree pruning for PageIndex (pre-filters documents by BM25 relevance)

libraryComponents.description: Component library reference (for Code Mode compatibility)

measuredAtomically.description:
Whether both sides were read in the one request that also applied the
patch (larql `apply_measured`). When false the readings were separate
requests, which on a multi-instance service can route to an instance
that never saw the apply.

scoreBefore.description: DESCRIBE gate score for the target edge before the edit; null if absent.

scoreAfter.description: Same, after. For a DELETE a clean suppression reads as null or ~0.

top1Before.description:
⚠️ Optional because they are NOT STORED on a sealed row — a top-1 token
echoes the target, so both strings live in {@link LarqlSubject}. They are
still populated in memory by `computeOutputShift`, which is where the
sealing step reads them from before they are stripped for persistence.

top1Changed.description: Whether the argmax moved. Coarse: a reordering below rank 1 leaves it false.

totalVariation.description: Share of probability mass that moved, in [0,1].

k.description: k compared, so a reader knows the resolution behind the number.

issuerUrl.description: OIDC issuer URL (e.g., https://acme.okta.com) — used for OIDC Discovery

authorizationEndpoint.description: Manual authorization endpoint (if no OIDC Discovery)

jwksUri.description: Manual JWKS URI for token signature validation

clientId.description: OAuth client ID registered with the admin's IdP

clientSecretRef.description: Reference to client secret stored in Infisical (e.g., "WL_{id}_IDP_CLIENT_SECRET")

scopeMapping.description: Map admin IdP scopes to DiVinci MCP scopes

userMapping.description: User attribute mapping from IdP claims to DiVinci user context

allowedRedirectUris.description: Allowed redirect URIs for this whitelabel's MCP clients

enabled.description: Whether MCP is enabled for this whitelabel's releases

billingMode.description: Who pays for MCP tool calls: admin = whitelabel owner, end-user = authenticated user

globalRateLimit.description: Global rate limits for all MCP access to this whitelabel

ragVectorId.description:
The RAG vector (collection) the chunk was retrieved from. Stamped only when
a group retrieval is asked to (GroupContextOptions.tagSourceCollection), so
the public API can say which member index each merged chunk came from.

isCTA.description:
ChatCTA signal: set by the post-generation CTA matcher (generateChatCTAs)
when the reply text matched an active release CTA's trigger keywords. The
embed/web client renders a block-level CTACard from these fields (mirrors
the isProduct decoration path, but block-level, not an inline span swap).

ctaWhitelabelId.description:
email-gated-download render config. NOTE: the gated `assetUrl` is
deliberately NOT included here — leaking it pre-submit would defeat the
gate. The client renders the inline form from these fields and receives
`assetUrl` from the submit endpoint's response after a successful capture.

matchText.description:
Span-anchoring (productSubReplies.spanAnchoring): the EXACT prose span the
server resolved to this product/search, so the client decorates that span
verbatim instead of re-deriving matches from `productName`. When present,
the client anchors on `matchText` and shows `productName` in the popover.

productKind.description:
"product" → links to a catalog product; "search" → links to a shop search
query (generic category / unresolved rename).

stale.description:
True when a refresh found the product missing from its catalog; the
bubble still renders a plain link to the last-known url.

linkedProduct.description:
Admin-curated link from this chunk's source document to a sellable catalog
product (RagVectorFile2.linkedProduct, denormalized at enrich time). The
chat context bubble renders a buy affordance from this. catalogId/productId
are the canonical reference; title/url/imageUrl render without a round-trip.

contentImages.description: Content images found in this chunk's text (R2-hosted images from crawled pages)

tileImages.description:
Rendered page images (PixelRAG visual lane), attached at read time by
enrich-source-info. Become image_url parts on the user turn.

sourceUrl.description: Original source URL for this chunk's document (e.g., YouTube URL, crawled page URL, user-provided link)

linkUrl.description:
Operator MANUAL link (file- or chunk-level, set via set-link). The
highest-priority citation link — preferred over linkedProduct.url and
sourceUrl. `linkTitle` overrides the displayed citation title.

mediaType.description: Media type — set for audio/video source documents

similarity.description:
Raw vector similarity score (typically 0–1) from retrieval. Threaded
through hydration so the cross-index reranker can globally rank chunks
merged from multiple vectors by relevance before trimming to top-N.
Absent on chunks that lost their score (e.g. compression-merged blobs).

manualRankScore.description:
Blended manual-priority score (similarity + manualPriority + bounded
recency) from the per-vector ranker. The cross-index reranker prefers this
over raw `similarity` so an operator's manualPriority/recency boost survives
a multi-vector group merge instead of being flattened back to relevance.

pinned.description:
True when this chunk was force-included by the manual-priority HARD pin.
The cross-index reranker exempts pinned chunks from the top-N trim so an
operator pin survives even against higher-similarity chunks from other
vectors.

compressedFromSources.description:
When context compression merges multiple chunks into a single text blob,
this field records all contributing source documents (not just the first).
Present only on items where vectorId === "compressed".

level.description: Tree level: 0 = leaf (original chunk), 1+ = summary nodes

isSummary.description: Whether this node is an LLM-generated cluster summary

clusterId.description: Cluster ID the node belongs to at its level

raptorMetadata.description:
RAPTOR retrieval provenance — set on chunks returned from RAPTOR vectors.
Lets callers/clients distinguish leaf chunks from LLM-generated summary
nodes and reason about which abstraction level surfaced the result.
Only populated when the originating vector uses vectorIndexTool === "raptor".

toolId.description:
`ext:<whitelabelId>:<slug>` — the registration, never the endpoint URL.
Deliberately the ONLY field: it is ours, and the registration behind it
is where a vendor name is read from. Copying a name out of the vendor's
own response would let the third party author the record that says a
third party authored this.

externalSource.description: This text came from a THIRD PARTY, not from the workspace's own corpus.

kind.description: Which primitive this edit is — what the receipt certifies. See {@link EDIT_KIND_LEGEND}.

readings.description: The before/after top-k behind `outputShift`, on the prompt it was read with.

gateEvidence.description: Deterministic gate-space record — the primary evidence for the edit.

outputShift.description:
Whether the edit moved the walk path's next-token distribution for the
probe prompt, and by how much. Absent when either snapshot failed —
never zero, which would read as "nothing moved".

slots.description: INSERT only: every (layer, feature) the constellation insert claimed.

insertMode.description: INSERT only: `knn`, `constellation` (gate from a live residual) or `embedding` fallback.

kind.description:
Which primitive this row is — see {@link LarqlEditKind}. Stamped at
commit from `op` and what larql reported. Absent on rows written before
the field existed; readers derive it for those (a DELETE is always
`ffn_delete`; an INSERT is `output_override` iff its wire patch carries
an `insert_knn` operation) rather than treating absence as a kind.

insertMode.description: INSERT only: the mode larql reported for the insert.

entity.description:
⚠️ Present only on LEGACY rows written before subject sealing, and on rows
written with no encryption secret configured. New rows carry
{@link LarqlPatchProps.sealedSubject} instead and leave these absent — read
a subject through `openLarqlSubject`, never off these fields directly.

subjectFingerprint.description:
Salted digest of (entity, relation, target). Safe to expose on a receipt,
in a dossier, and to a supervisory authority.

subjectSealed.description:
False or absent means the subject is in plaintext on this row (a legacy
row, or one written before the secret was provisioned). Never assume
sealed — a receipt must refuse to mint from an unsealed row rather than
publish the subject it is attesting to erasing.

larqlRuntime.description:
Identifier of the LarQL runtime that applied this edit — the deployed
image tag, e.g. "b20ff753-2017b761" (vindex sha + larql commit).

readingsMeta.description:
The non-identifying half of {@link LarqlEditReadings}, kept in the clear so
a receipt can state the resolution of the measurement — k, whether both
sides were read atomically, how many prompts — without opening the seal.

slots.description:
INSERT only: every (layer, feature) the constellation insert claimed.
`layer` / `feature` above carry the first slot so older readers keep
working; an insert spans one feature per knowledge layer.

wirePatch.description:
INSERT only: the patch larql installed, gate and down vectors included,
exactly as `POST /v1/insert` returned it. Hydration and replay re-apply
this verbatim through `/v1/patches/apply`, so a rebuilt overlay carries
the same vectors the edit was measured with — re-running the insert
would capture a fresh residual and could land elsewhere.

restoredFrom.description:
Set on rows a version restore re-created: the version restored from and
the row that carried this patch when that version was taken.

modelPrompt.description: The exact text the model was run with, after prompt-style wrapping.

override.description:
Set when an added fact (a `knn` INSERT) supplied the answer: larql puts
that token first at probability 1.0 and keeps the model's own top-k after
it. Absent when the forward pass answered on its own.

enabled.description: Dark-launch flag. Multi-AI is OFF unless this is explicitly true.

maxTurnsPerMessage.description: Hard cap on AI turns per user message (platform-clamped to <= 12; default 6).

exchangeBudgetNanoUSD.description: Hard per-exchange spend ceiling in nanoUSD — ~4x a normal reply (platform-clamped).

perTurnMaxOutputTokens.description: Per-turn output-token clamp passed to each generation. Omit for the model default.

maxExchangeMs.description: Hard per-exchange wall-clock ceiling in ms (platform-clamped to <= 180000; default 90000).

loopWindow.description: Recent-turn window for semantic-loop detection (0 disables; default 4).

message.description: Short markdown-friendly line shown in the Divinci Agent transcript.

imageUrl.description: Public image URL (favicon, page image, etc.) for markdown embeds.

urls.description: Sample / inventory URLs for this surface (capped).

summary.description: One or two sentences, in plain language, about what this business does.

audience.description: Who the site appears to be speaking to.

tone.description: How the site sounds — "plain and technical", "warm and informal".

offerings.description: Concrete things the site offers. Bounded; display truncates further.

confidence.description:
How much evidence this rests on. `low` means URL structure only — the UI
says so, because a confident-sounding guess from path names is exactly
the kind of thing that destroys trust when it is wrong.

basis.description: What the pass was derived from, for the UI's "based on…" line.

revision.description: Increments per pass, so the client can animate a revision.

resources.description: Which resources to sync. Defaults to session notes + protocols + forms.

targetVectorId.description: The RagVector this connector ingests into.

consultantIds.description:
Restrict to these Practice Better consultant IDs. Empty/absent means the
whole practice. Use this so a clinician's release covers only their own
caseload rather than every colleague's clients.

teamFor.description: Maps to the API's `team_for` param: "all" | "me" | a consultant id.

ownerFiltering.description: Scope patient retrieval to the asking practitioner's own records.

dailyRequestBudget.description:
Requests/day this connector may spend against the practice's shared
10,000/day quota. The sync stops cleanly and resumes next cycle rather than
consuming the customer's whole budget. Default 2,000.

autoSync.description: Recurring sync on/off; mirrored onto syncConfig.

webhookSubscriptionId.description: Practice Better webhook subscription id, set by setupWebhook.

webhookSigningSecret.description:
Secret material for the webhook. `webhookSigningSecret` is returned by
Practice Better on subscribe (`plaintextSigningSecret`);
`webhookVerificationToken` is one WE generate and assert on delivery.
Both are encrypted at rest by connection/encryption.ts — never log either.

baseUrl.description:
Override the API base URL, so the connector can be pointed at the local mock
Practice Better server for demos and tests. Permitted only in local/test/dev
environments — see resolveBaseUrl().

enabled.description:
Master on/off. Unset → falls back to the PRODUCT_SUB_REPLIES_ENABLED env
var (default on) for backwards compatibility.

retroMatch.description:
Retroactively scan the LLM's main response text for product mentions and
surface a sub-reply/decoration even when the product chunk wasn't included
in the RAG context this turn.

maxProducts.description: Max distinct products surfaced per reply. Default 1.

matchThreshold.description: Score threshold in [0,1] a product must clear to be surfaced. Default 0.5.

shopFallback.description: Link product-style labels that match no specific product to a shop search.

shopSearchUrlTemplate.description:
Shop search URL template; `{q}` is replaced with the URL-encoded span,
e.g. "https://shop.drfuhrman.com/search.php?search_query={q}".

strongThreshold.description: Min score in [0,1] to link a span to a specific product. Default 0.85.

spanAnchoring.description:
Server-side product SPAN ANCHORING (Phase 2): for each product-mention span
in the reply, resolve the exact catalog product (or a shop search) server-
side and hand the client the exact span + URL — so renames, SKU-titled books,
and generic categories decorate without the client re-guessing from the
canonical title. Default off; ships behind this flag.

minWeight.description: Min prominenceOf for the generic-question prominence fallback. Default 0.5.

minRelevance.description:
Min BM25 relevance (0-1) for a product to count as relevant to the
question. Default 0.3. Higher → fewer, more on-topic injections.

prominenceAlpha.description:
Prominence-boost strength (multiplicative α) applied when ranking the
injected products. Default 0.25 (a featured product gets up to +25%).
Raise (e.g. 0.5–1) to let storefront prominence outrank a somewhat-more-
relevant product in the recommendation list.

featuredInPrompt.description:
Inject the catalog's most storefront-prominent products into the AI's
GENERATION context (not just post-hoc decoration) so the assistant prefers
recommending the featured items. Closes the gap where prominence only
affected decoration/ranking, never which products the AI actually names.
Default off; needs prominence weights (from the landing-page crawl).

allowedCategories.description:
Llama Guard codes to treat as SAFE for this Release (e.g. `["S6"]` for a
medical-device or legal assistant). Codes outside
WAIVABLE_HARM_CATEGORIES are ignored — a release cannot opt out of the
floor. A flagged message is blocked unless EVERY category it tripped is
waived, so "S6" alone still blocks "S6,S1".

effectiveAssistantId.description:
Assistant actually used for this run. Backed by
`assistantAttribution.used`. Kept at the top level for compatibility
with existing report renderers.

effectiveJudgeToolId.description: Judge model used for scoring in this run. Null when no LLM scorer ran.

response.description:
Debug surface — what the model actually generated + the RAG chunks
that were retrieved and injected. Without these, "this variant scored
0 on item X" is unactionable: the caller can't tell whether the
model returned garbage, the retrieval missed, or the judge rubric
is mismatched. With them, the caller can diff variants and see
exactly why one passed and another didn't.

answerText.description: The external system's reply, verbatim. Rendered as text only, never as HTML.

variantId.description: The variant key used in reports: `target:<targetId>`.

skippedScorers.description: Scorers on the suite that this run did NOT run, and why (no retrieval context for an external system).

judge.description:
What judged this run. A figure is only comparable to another produced under
the same judge and rubric, so both are recorded with the result.

mode.description: "imported": answers were supplied. "live": we asked the target.

live.description: Live runs only: what happened when we asked.

sourceNote.description: Free text from the importer: where the answers came from and when. Data, never instructions.

report.description: MultiReleaseReport for this one variant. Mixed: the builder owns the shape.

pairs.description: Questions scored for BOTH variants. Others are excluded, not counted as 0.

excluded.description: Questions where either variant has no score.

meanDiff.description: meanA - meanB over the paired questions.

wallClockMs.description:
Total wall-clock duration of the entire suite run for this release,
in milliseconds. Includes batching/concurrency overhead. Useful for
RAG-Arena throughput comparisons (e.g. prod NF4 vs DFlash spec-decode).

unscoredCount.description:
Tests whose answer was generated but that NO scorer scored (every scorer
failed, or every scorer was skipped). Not passed, not errored, and never
averaged in as 0. `testCount = passedCount + unscoredCount + errorCount`.
See `unscored` for why each one has no score.

partiallyScoredCount.description: Scored tests where at least one scorer failed, so the score used a subset of scorers.

resumedCount.description: Tests carried from an earlier run of the same pass (`iterationResultId` option) rather than run now.

llmMs.description: Per-test wall-clock duration in ms (includes RAG retrieval + LLM + scoring).

answerMs.description: Time to produce the answer (retrieval + generation, no scoring); absent when not recorded.

scorerFailures.description: Scorers that failed on this test; present only when some did.

reasons.description: Why each scorer produced nothing, e.g. "llm-factual-consistency-vs-reference: error: Gemini API error: 429".

rhoLowerTarget.description:
The 95% CI lower-bound floor a judge must clear to count as
defensibly calibrated. Range [0, 1]. Higher = stricter.

calibrationConfig.description:
Per-suite calibration risk profile. Different suites have different
stakes (clinical Q&A → strict; marketing copy → loose). When unset,
the platform default applies (rhoLowerTarget=0.70, rhoTargetN=30).

excludedReleaseIds.description:
Per-suite release-exclusion deny list. Variants whose `releaseId`
appears in this array are filtered out of the calibration queue
for THIS suite. Used when a release is known to produce garbled /
useless responses (e.g. a fine-tune that diverged) so its
variants don't waste rater time on every Q/A. Other suites in
the workspace are unaffected (per-suite scope).

heldOut.description:
Held-out test set: its questions must never be published. No TrustBench
run on this suite may be made public while this is set
(server-resources trustbench/publication-gates.ts). Set or cleared via
PUT /:whitelabelId/scored-qa/suites/:suiteId/held-out, which records who
and when below.

chunkingTool.description: The chunker this file was split with.

ragSourceId.description: Reference to the top-level RagVectorSource that this file belongs to.

sourceUrl.description: Original source URL for this file (e.g., YouTube link, external document URL)

vectorIndexProcessing.description:
Work-queue tracker: which RagVector ObjectIds (24-char hex) still need to
process this file. Cleared on status → COMPLETED. Entries are strictly
ragVector `_id` strings.

embeddingLocks.description:
Transient reservation locks held during inline embedding generation
(`vectorProcessReserve` / `vectorProcessRelease` in
`ensure-embedings.ts`). Entries are tool ID strings like
`"cloudflare-v2"`, `"qdrant"`, `"lightrag"`. Released on successful
completion OR on failure — may leak if the process crashes mid-reserve.
Separate from `vectorIndexProcessing` so each field has a single,
predictable semantics (Tier B #7, 2026-04-21).

previousState.description: Optional terminal state the prior event left the file in (for auditing transitions).

correlationId.description: Groups events from one logical operation — e.g. all file-touches inside a fix-all cycle.

treeSearchModel.description:
PageIndex node selector for member vectors, overriding each vector's own
treeSearchModel (e.g. "typesafe/jev-two-stage"). Unset = each vector's own.

halfLifeDays.description: Exponential-decay half-life in days, >= 1. Unset → default (180).

id.description: auth0 userId | workflow run id | script name | fix-all operationId

label.description: Optional display name (e.g. email) for quick triage.

botName.description: Default bot display name in meetings

pinned.description:
Shared (whitelabel-level) pin. A pinned release floats to the top of the
release list for ALL users of the whitelabel. Toggled via the editConfig-
gated POST /:releaseId/pin route.

autoSyncGenerated.description:
True when this draft was forked automatically by the connector auto-sync
changelog roll-up (so the roll-up can avoid stacking duplicate drafts
without blocking on unrelated manual drafts).

requireSignedAnonymousChat.description:
When true, anonymous-chat requests for this release MUST carry a valid
`X-Landing-Page-Ts` / `X-Landing-Page-Sig` HMAC pair (signed by the
landing-page worker under the shared `LANDING_PAGE_HMAC_KEY`) or they
are rejected with 403. Default false = back-compat: missing/invalid
headers are ignored and the request passes through. See
verify-landing-page-hmac middleware in public-api.

fallbackAssistants.description:
Ordered fallback chain. When the primary `assistant` model returns a
retryable failure (provider 429 / capacity / 5xx / timeout), generation
retries with these models in order — first success wins. Empty/absent
means no fallback (today's behavior). Each entry is the same
{id, finetune} reference shape as the primary `assistant`.

rerankMaxChunks.description:
Per-release cap on chunks surviving the cross-index RAG merge-rerank before
the LLM (per-tenant override for the global RAG_RERANK_MAX_CHUNKS default).
Unset → env default (8); 0 → disabled (no trim).

ragTrigger.description:
Pre-emptive RAG gate (Tier 1). mode="heuristic" skips retrieval for messages
that don't need grounding (greetings/acks). Unset / "always" → always retrieve.

ragContextDisplayMode.description:
Display-only control for how RAG source-context bubbles render in chat.
Distinct from `requireRagContext` (which gates retrieval server-side):
  - "hidden" — no context bubbles
  - "title"  — bubbles show the cleaned chunk title only, no hover popup
  - "full"   — bubbles show title + hover popup (default / today's behavior)
Unset → treated as "full".

memory.description: Memory configuration override for this release

spendCapCentsPerDay.description:
Hard daily spend cap in US cents for this release (backstop for free,
public-facing releases like the homepage assistant). Unset → uncapped.
Enforced before escrow; resets at midnight UTC.

themeOverride.description:
Per-release theme override. When set, takes priority over the
whitelabel-level `theme` for this release only (resolved at the embed
`release-item` + public-share endpoints into the `_whitelabelTheme`
field the embed client already consumes). Absent/null → inherit the
whitelabel theme. Mirrors the responseTypeConfigOverride / ttsConfigOverride
per-release override convention.

pictureOverride.description:
Per-release avatar/logo URL. When set, takes priority over the
whitelabel-level `picture` for this release only (resolved at the
`release-item` / `releases-by-ids` endpoints into `_whitelabelPicture`,
which the chat avatar circle already consumes). Absent → inherit the
whitelabel picture. Same convention as themeOverride.

pricingTiers.description:
Paid, spend-based membership tiers defined ON this release. When non-empty,
this set OVERRIDES the white-label EmbedTier set for this release: an
end-user's active release-tier subscription determines their per-window
spend allowance on this release (window-unlock model — the release owner's
wallet still funds inference). Empty/absent → existing global EmbedTier
behavior. See ReleasePricingTier.

outputPipelineId.description: Pipeline ID for RAG output workflow (document retrieval)

productOutputPipelineId.description: Pipeline ID for product recommendation workflow

testingDomains.description:
Testing domains whitelist - messages from these domains won't count against quotas.
Supports exact domains (staging.example.com) and wildcard patterns (*.dev.example.com).

embeddingModelOverride.description:
Override embedding model for this release (inherits from white label if null).
Example: "gemini-embedding-001@1536", "@cf/baai/bge-base-en-v1.5"

vectorIndexToolOverride.description: Override vector database tool for this release (inherits from white label if null).

ttsToolOverride.description: Override TTS tool for this release (inherits from white label if null).

ttsVoiceOverride.description: Override TTS voice for this release (inherits from white label if null).

ttsConfigOverride.description: Override TTS configuration for this release (merges with white label config).

sttToolOverride.description:
Override STT (speech-to-text) tool for this release (inherits from white
label if null).

voiceTransport.description: Which Twilio architecture answers phone calls for this release.

avatar.description: Real-time video-avatar configuration (Runway Characters). Off if absent.

enabledMcpServerIds.description:
WhitelabelMcpServer ids whose tools are exposed to this release's chat
tool-loop. Connected + discovered at turn time, fail-open per server.

_brandingRequired.description: Whether "Powered by Divinci" branding is required (from WhiteLabel subscription). Defaults to true.

_helpRequestsEnabled.description:
Whether this release offers anonymous visitors a "talk to a person"
(help request) button. Computed by the public release-item endpoint from
`notificationFlaggers.helpRequests.enabled`, because the public payload's
field allowlist deliberately omits `notificationFlaggers` (its `custom[]`
titles are internal workflow names). Anonymous clients MUST gate on this,
not on notificationFlaggers, which they never receive.

autoFineTuneMinExamples.description: Minimum new captured edits required before auto-cron submits a run. Default 50.

stagedBy.description: "auto-cron" if M14 staged it; admin auth0 sub if surface staged it manually.

proposedAssistantConfig.description:
M15 — staging slot for newly-trained models awaiting admin approval.
pollTrainingRunStatus writes here when a FineTuneTrainingRun
transitions to `completed`. Admin reviews + manually copies the
resultModelId onto release.assistant to promote it into the live
chat path. Auto-attach is intentionally NOT default — production
traffic always passes through the human-approval gate.

slug.description: URL-friendly slug, unique within the release's tier array.

priceCents.description:
Operator-set price in the smallest currency unit (cents). 0/absent → free
tier (not purchasable, no Stripe price).

stripeProductId.description: Stripe Product id, written back by the price-sync step.

stripePriceId.description:
Stripe recurring Price id, written back by the price-sync step. Required
before an end-user can check out this tier.

isDefault.description:
The tier a logged-in-but-unpaid release user falls into. Exactly one tier
in the array should set this; the resolver falls back to the first tier.

durationMs.description: Time window duration in milliseconds (e.g. 86400000 = 1 day).

limitNanoUSD.description: Max allowed spend in nano-USD as a decimal string ("-1" = unlimited).

enabled.description:
Master switch. Off (or absent) → today's behavior: replies are fronted by
the release/white-label identity and notifications fan out white-label-wide.

userId.description: Stable identity id of the collaborator (Auth0 sub).

active.description:
Temporarily take someone out of rotation (vacation, left the team) without
losing their spot on the roster. Absent === active.

ttlSeconds.description: Cache entry TTL in seconds. Default 3600 (1h). Clamped [30, 86400].

similarityThreshold.description:
Cosine-similarity threshold [0,1] for a HIT. Higher = stricter (safer).
Default 0.97; clamped ≥0.9 for answer reuse (looser than that risks
serving a stored answer for a merely-related question).

enforcement.description: "advisory" = prompt guidance only; "strict" = strips disallowed content from responses

enabled.description: Enable RRF fusion when both BM25 and vector results available

k.description: RRF ranking constant (default: 60, from original RRF paper)

exactMatchBoost.description: Boost multiplier for exact keyword matches (default: 2.0)

enabled.description:
Master opt-in. THE WALL: when false (the default), deriveSiteActions
returns [] — the assistant gets zero executable site actions even though
the manifest is fully activated for knowledge/guidance.

allowedCategories.description: Categories the customer permits. Default: navigation only.

allowList.description: Whitelist mode: if non-empty, ONLY these action names are derivable.

blockList.description: Action names to exclude (applied after allowList).

forms.description:
Notable forms across the site (route + handle), for navigation guidance and
(v1.5) mutation actions. `fields` carries the per-page form fields up so
submit actions can be parameterized; absent on older manifests.

enabled.description:
Master switch for this release's tool/skill loop. When true, qualifying
turns route to the tool-calling model and run the native loop with the
selected skills; when false the loop never runs regardless of what skills
are configured.

catalogSkills.description:
Enabled catalog skills. Key: WhitelabelSkill._id. Value: the subset of that
skill's action names (SkillIntegration.skillActions[].name) exposed to this
release's loop; an empty array → ALL of that skill's actions. A skill is
enabled if it's id is a key here.

mcpSkills.description:
Enabled MCP skills. Key: MCPSkillInfo._id (a connected MCP server). Value:
the subset of that server's MCPSkillTool._id values exposed to this
release's loop; an empty array → ALL of that server's active tools. A
server is enabled iff its id is a key here.

maxToolIterations.description:
Maximum number of tool-call / reflection iterations the model may take in a
single chat turn before the loop is forced to stop.

toolCallingAssistant.description:
The single assistant that serves this release's tool loop. No BYOK
override (`authId`) — always resolved via the platform default key; the
client is billed for actual usage through the normal escrow regardless of
which literal key served the call. Required (enforced by
toolCallingAssistantValidator at save time) whenever `enabled` is true;
the referenced assistant must implement native tool calling, checked
against the catalog rather than trusting a declarative flag alone. When a
release enables the loop without setting this explicitly, it defaults
server-side to the release's own primary assistant — which then must
itself support tool calling, or the save is rejected.

fallbackToolCallingAssistants.description:
Ordered fallback chain for the tool loop, mirroring
`Release.fallbackAssistants` for the primary assistant. When
`toolCallingAssistant` returns a RETRYABLE failure (provider 429 /
capacity / 5xx / timeout — same `isRetryableModelError` classification the
main chain uses) the loop retries with these, in order; first success wins.

mode.description:
"model-default": inherit the set implied by the release's model.
"custom": use `codes` exactly.

codes.description: BCP-47 codes when mode = "custom". Ignored for "model-default".

retrievalMs.description:
Retrieval wall-clock for this answer: the slowest vector, because
prepareContext queries every vector in one Promise.all. null when no
vector recorded a time; absent on reports built before 2026-10-27.

matchedMessageId.description: First message whose content matched `search`, when applicable.

isLinear.description: See linearity.ts — absent/false both mean "not linear" (branched).

content.description: Model text output this turn (may be empty on pure tool-call turns).

createdAt.description:
When the turn started (ms since epoch). Read by stale-pending recovery to
tell a leaked entry from a live one — without it the two are
indistinguishable, and the sub-schema has `_id: false` so there is no
ObjectId to recover a timestamp from either.

isLinear.description:
True when this transcript is a strictly LINEAR conversation: every
chat-participating message (user/assistant/error — `social` and `system`
are excluded) replies to its immediate predecessor, so array order IS
conversational order and no branch exists.

release.description:
Task #188 (2026-05-27): ObjectId of the WhiteLabelRelease this chat was
started against. Used by resolveMessageEnvironment to load THE one
release for config (replacing per-field heuristic lookups that caused
Bug 15/16/17/18/19). Optional/undefined for:
  - legacy transcripts created before this field existed
  - non-release chats (Divinci Agent panel, eval-harness, scoring suites)
For those, the existing per-field heuristic fallback path applies.
Sub-thread transcripts inherit the parent's release at creation time
(Phase 2 wire-up).

userId.description:
Explicit authorship for human-authored messages (`role: "user"` and
`role: "social"`). Holds the sender's stable identity id (auth0 sub,
`apikey:*`, or embed API-key user id) — the same value historically
overloaded onto `name`. Added so multiplayer chats can reliably
attribute "who said what" without conflating identity with the
display label in `name`.

displayName.description:
Human-readable label for the sender identified by `userId` (their Auth0
nickname, or the equivalent resolved via `getUserById`). Purely cosmetic —
never used for attribution/lookups (that's `userId` / `name`, see above).
Exists so multi-user transcripts (multiple people talking to the same
assistant in one thread) can tell the model WHO is speaking on each turn,
not just that turns come from different ids. Optional + additive; absent
on messages written before this field landed and on AI/system/error
messages.

pictureUrl.description:
Picture URL for the sender identified by `userId` — mirrors `displayName`
above (same cosmetic-only contract, same optional/additive shape, resolved
once at send time from a staff member's per-whitelabel
WhitelabelUserProfile picture or the whitelabel's default appearance).

onBehalfOfOwner.description:
True when this human-authored ("user") message was sent by an authorized
staff member speaking on behalf of the release/whitelabel owner — not
typed by the actual end customer (see addPrivledgedAIMessage, the
Customer Chats "reply as company" flow). Unlike `displayName` (cosmetic
only), this is surfaced to the LLM as explicit platform metadata (see
transcriptToAssistantInput) so the model doesn't mistake an authoritative
company reply for ordinary customer input — on the live turn AND on
replay, so history stays accurate. Optional + additive; absent means
"ordinary customer/user message."

assistantId.description:
Explicit AI authorship for `role: "assistant"` (and `"error"`) messages —
the stable id of the model/assistant that produced the message
(`assistantAPI.tool.id`, the same identifier Arena variants and
side-agents record). This is the AI analog of `userId`: it lets a chat
attribute "which AI said this", which conversational multi-AI requires.

provenance.description:
Where an `assistant` message's text was generated. `"local"` = produced on
the visitor's device via delegated inference (the release only ACCEPTED +
signed the text, it did not AUTHOR it); `"cloud"` / absent = release-
authored. Carried across the anonymous→owned handoff so a delegated turn is
NOT silently laundered into a release-authored one when claimed into an
owned chat. Renderers should mark a `"local"` turn as on-device, not present
it as authoritative assistant output. Optional + additive.

citedSources.description:
Sources the answer actually CITES, in order of first citation — derived
from its `[N]` markers against the citation manifest (the ordered list the
model was shown as `[Source 1..N]`). Deliberately NOT the retrieval union:
retrieval routinely surfaces documents the answer never uses, and listing
those attributes claims to documents that were never cited.

arenaVariants.description: Arena mode: array of model variant responses for side-by-side comparison

arenaSelectedIndex.description: Arena mode: index of the user's chosen response variant

arenaStreamingStatus.description: Arena streaming: "streaming" while variants are still arriving, "complete" when done

arenaExpectedVariants.description: Arena streaming: how many variants are expected (for rendering skeletons)

optimisticId.description:
Bug 201 (2026-05-27): client-supplied id used for React-key reconciliation
between the optimistic message (rendered immediately on send) and the
server-assigned message returned via WebSocket. When set, the React
key should prefer this over `_id` so the optimistic→real transition
doesn't re-key + re-mount the subtree (which caused Bug 25 placeholder
flicker + Bug 27 avatar flicker). Optional, additive — old messages
without it still render correctly.

llmRewrittenRuleIds.description: Rules rewritten by the tier-2 LLM span rewriter (guideline-driven).

redactedRuleIds.description: Guardrail rules whose span was redacted (fail-to-redaction, not open).

suppressed.description: True iff a failClosed guardrail suppressed the whole reply.

styleRewrite.description:
Style-pattern rewrite audit: present iff this response was rewritten
by the Phase 4 pipeline. `content` holds the rewritten text;
`originalContent` here is the pre-rewrite version. Lets admins
inspect + roll back individual rewrites without re-running detect.
`deferredMatchRuleIds` captures rules that matched but had no
`substitutionTemplate` — accumulates training data for the
eventual T2 LLM-rewrite path.

toolLoop.description:
Tool-loop execution state for skill confirmation flows.
Present on assistant messages that triggered one or more skill tool calls.
Iterations are appended as the loop progresses; the client renders
confirmation buttons based on each iteration's status.

userInfo.description:
Ambient context the client supplied at send time — timezone, and
eventually coarse location. Stored on the message so historical
thread replays can include the same context the model originally saw.
Only present on role:"user" messages.

streamingEnabled.description: Enable WebSocket streaming for supported providers

mode.description: "crawl" follows links from rootUrl; "feed" ingests an explicit sitemap/URL list.

rootUrl.description: Crawl root (mode=crawl) — may be a deep subpath.

feedUrl.description: Feed source (mode=feed): a sitemap.xml or a URL-list/JSON feed.

feedUrls.description:
Explicit URL list (mode=feed): when set, these URLs are scraped directly
instead of fetching+parsing feedUrl. feedUrl is still required as the feed's
stable identity/source key. Lets a connector ingest a known set of pages
(e.g. drfuhrman's gated /recipes/print-recipe?id=<id> URLs) without hosting a
feed file. Each URL is still SSRF-revalidated before scraping.

targetVectorId.description: The RagVector this connector ingests into. May be shared across connectors.

limit.description: Max pages to traverse (mode=crawl). Maps to crawlConfig.limit.

allowedPaths.description: Restrict the crawl to these path prefixes (scopes a subpath root).

validGetParameters.description: Query-string params that distinguish URLs (others stripped for dedup).

runSitemap.description: Parse + follow sitemap.xml during a crawl.

crawlSubdomains.description:
(mode=crawl) Follow links to sub-domains of the root's registrable domain
(eTLD+1) — e.g. crawl videos.example.org + shop.example.org as part of an
example.org crawl. Each sub-domain's own robots.txt is respected. Default
false (exact-origin).

buildProductCatalog.description:
(mode=crawl) After the crawl, scan every crawled page's schema.org
JSON-LD for `@type: Product` entities and build/refresh this whitelabel's
product catalog from them (title, price, image, description, category,
sku). Deterministic + free (JSON-LD is already parsed at scrape time); no
per-page LLM classification. Default false.

scraperTool.description: Scraper tool id (defaults to the WWW-RAG fetch-scraper).

loginUrl.description: Form-POST login endpoint (same origin as the crawl root).

scrapeAuth.description: Member-auth for gated sites. Secret fields encrypted at rest.

stripCrossPageBoilerplate.description:
(mode=feed) Strip cross-page boilerplate (site nav/header/footer/CTA that
repeats across the feed's pages) before chunking. Runs a first pass that
scrapes every feed URL to learn the recurring template, then strips it from
each page on the real ingest pass. Doubles scrape cost for the run, so it's
opt-in — use it for template-heavy sites (e.g. drfuhrman recipe print pages)
where the shared chrome would otherwise pollute every chunk. Crawl mode
strips inline and ignores this flag. Needs >= 4 URLs to judge.

dropReviewComments.description:
(langextract chunker) Drop user review/comment chunks (star ratings +
casual testimonial text with no recipe/content signal) that scraped review
sections add as retrieval noise. Off by default; opt-in for recipe/review
corpora. Passed to the chunker via resolveCrawlTools.

scraperRenderJs.description:
(cloudflare-browser scraper) JS rendering mode. Default true (SPA sites).
Set false for SERVER-rendered targets like drfuhrman print-recipe pages,
where a full browser render loads the site shell and buries the recipe —
the raw authenticated HTML is the clean printable content. The auth cookie
applies either way (sent as an HTTP header). Ignored by other scrapers.

syncIntervalMinutes.description: Recurrence cadence in minutes (the "cadence" setting); default daily.

swapOnSuccess.description:
When the target vector is attached to a published (AVAILABLE) release,
crawl into a fresh same-config draft vector instead of failing the
"can't update vector when used" guard, then repoint every AVAILABLE
release referencing the original vector to the draft once the crawl
succeeds. The draft vector's id also becomes this connection's stored
targetVectorId, so a recurring (autoSync) connector keeps swapping onto
a fresh draft each cycle. On failure the abandoned draft is deleted and
the live release is untouched. Off by default — swapping a customer's
live knowledge base unattended is a deliberate opt-in, not a default.

post.summary: POST /api/v1/releases/:releaseId/deprecate — Take a PUBLISHED release out of service. The counterpart to /publish, which had no inverse on this surface: `DELETE /:releaseId` only removes DRAFTS, so an API-key client could publish a release and then had no way to withdraw it.  This is the withdrawal path for a rights refusal. WWW-RAG re-checks robots.txt before every crawl, but a host that ALLOWED AI use when we crawled it and refuses today was already published — and the only remedy is to stop serving it. Fifteen such sites were live on 2026-08-18 (Cloudflare's Managed robots.txt block names CloudflareBrowserRenderingCrawler, our exact crawler).  Deprecating rather than deleting is deliberate: the release stops serving (the public endpoint and the WWW-RAG directory both treat only `available` and `active` as live) while the record of what we published, and that we withdrew it, survives. A hard delete would destroy the evidence that the refusal was honoured.  ⚠️ Gated by `release:deprecate`, NOT `release:write`. Every other route on this surface acts on a DRAFT; this one retires a LIVE release, so a key that can publish must not be able to take a site down as a side effect. Pinned by scripts/ci/tests/test_release_auth_boundary.py.
